page: Microsoft Azure F4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Fasv6 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachment.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing also demonstrates strong performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while cached read-only small block memory bandwidth is average at 590.47 GB/sec, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, registering at 37.88 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.0 GB/sec.

For workloads, the F4as_v6 is suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, and moderate web serving, where it achieves a static web serving throughput of 8.39 GB/sec. It can handle light database operations and small-scale LLM inference, processing 1109.18 tokens/sec for a 135M model prompt, though performance drops significantly on larger models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide reliable compute performance without hyperthreading overhead, making it a stable choice for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-capacity uncached memory throughput.
